{{Short description|Riemannian manifold equipped with a differential p-form}}
{{MOS|article|[[MOS:MATH]] - needs to use {{tl|math}} for HTML variables and formulas|date=April 2026}}
In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[differential geometry]], a '''calibrated manifold''' is a [[Riemannian manifold]] (''M'',''g'') of dimension ''n'' equipped with a [[differential form|differential ''p''-form]] ''&phi;'' (for some 0 ≤ ''p'' ≤ ''n'') which is a '''calibration,''' meaning that:
* ''&phi;'' is [[Closed and exact differential forms|closed]], that is, d''&phi;'' = 0, where d is the [[exterior derivative]].
* ''&phi;'' has [[operator norm]] at most 1.  That is, for any ''x'' ∈ ''M'' and any [[multivector|''p''-vector]] <math>\xi \in \Lambda^p T_x M</math>, we have ''&phi;''(''&xi;'')&nbsp;≤&nbsp;vol(''&xi;''), with volume defined with respect to the Riemannian metric ''g''.
A main reason for defining a calibration is that it creates a distinguished set of "directions" (i.e. ''p''-planes) in which ''&phi;'' is actually equal to the volume form, that is, the inequality above is an equality.  For ''x'' in ''M'', set ''G''<sub>''x''</sub>(''&phi;'') to be the subset of such planes in the [[Grassmannian]] of ''p''-planes in T''<sub>x</sub>M''.  In cases of interest, ''G''<sub>''x''</sub>(''&phi;'') is always nonempty. Let ''G''(''&phi;'') be the union of ''G''<sub>''x''</sub>(''&phi;'') for all <math>x \in M</math>, viewed as a subspace of the bundle of ''p''-planes in T''M''.

==History==

[[F. Reese Harvey|Harvey]] and [[H. Blaine Lawson|Lawson]] introduced the term ''calibration'' and developed the theory in 1982,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Harvey |first1=Reese |author-link1=F. Reese Harvey |last2=Lawson |first2=H. Blaine |author-link2=H. Blaine Lawson |title=Calibrated geometries |journal=[[Acta Mathematica]] |date=1982 |volume=148 |issue=0 |pages=47–157 |doi=10.1007/BF02392726}}</ref> but the subject has a long prehistory.<ref name="Morgan">{{citation|title=Geometric Measure Theory: a Beginner's Guide|last=Morgan|first= Frank |author-link=Frank Morgan (mathematician) |edition=4th |publisher=Academic Press | location=London|year=2009 | pages=74–75 | ISBN=978-0-12-374444-9}}</ref>

The first motivating example, that of Kähler manifolds, is due implicitly to [[Wilhelm Wirtinger|Wirtinger]] in 1936<ref>{{citation | first = W. | last = Wirtinger | title = Eine Determinantenidentität und ihre Anwendung auf analytische Gebilde und Hermitesche Massbestimmung| journal = Monatshefte für Mathematik und Physik | volume = 44 | year = 1936 | pages = 343&ndash;365 (§6.5) | doi = 10.1007/BF01699328| s2cid = 121050865 }}.</ref> and explicitly to [[Georges de Rham|de Rham]] in 1957.<ref>{{citation | first = Georges | last = de Rham |author-link=Georges de Rham | title = On the Area of Complex Manifolds. Notes for the Seminar on Several Complex Variables| publisher=Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, New Jersey|year=1957–1958 }}.</ref>  In 1965, [[Herbert Federer|Federer]] used this to construct the first examples of singular minimal submanifolds.<ref name="Federer">{{citation | first = Herbert | last = Federer |author-link=Herbert Federer | title = Some theorems on integral currents| journal = Transactions of the American Mathematical Society | volume = 117 | year = 1965 | pages = 43&ndash;67 | doi = 10.2307/1994196 | jstor = 1994196| doi-access = free }}.</ref>

Soon afterwards, the other main examples were introduced. [[Edmond Bonan]] studied [[G2 manifold|G<sub>2</sub>-manifold]]s and  [[Spin(7)-manifold]]s in 1966,<ref>{{cite journal | first = Edmond| last =Bonan |author-link=Edmond Bonan| title = Sur les variétés riemanniennes à groupe d'holonomie G<sub>2</sub> ou Spin(7)| journal = [[Comptes rendus de l'Académie des Sciences|C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris]] | volume =262| year = 1966  | pages = 127&ndash;129 |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k6236863n/f141.item}}</ref> constructing all the parallel forms and showing that such manifolds must be [[Ricci-flat]], although examples of either would not be constructed for another 20 years until the work of [[Robert Bryant (mathematician)|Robert Bryant]]. [[Quaternion-Kähler manifold]]s were studied simultaneously in 1965 by [[Edmond Bonan]]<ref>{{cite journal | first =Edmond| last =Bonan |author-link=Edmond Bonan| title =Structure presque quaternale sur une variété différentiable| journal = [[Comptes rendus de l'Académie des Sciences|C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris]] | volume =260 | year = 1965 | pages =5445&ndash;5448 |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k4020b/f830.item}}</ref> and Vivian Yoh Kraines,<ref>{{cite journal | first =Vivian Yoh | last = Kraines | title = Topology of quaternionic manifolds
| journal = Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.| volume =71,3, 1 | year = 1965  | issue = 3 | pages = 526&ndash;527 | doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1965-11316-7| doi-access = free}}</ref> each of whom constructed the parallel 4-form.  Finally, in 1970, [[Marcel Berger|Berger]] gave the general argument that calibrated submanifolds are minimal and applied it to these cases.<ref>{{citation | first = Marcel | last = Berger |author-link=Marcel Berger | title = Quelques problèmes de géométrie riemannienne ou Deux variations sur les espaces symétriques compacts de rang un| journal = [[L'Enseignement mathématique]] | volume = 16 | year = 1970 | pages = 73&ndash;96 | url=https://www.e-periodica.ch/digbib/view?pid=ens-001%3A1970%3A16%3A%3A228 }}, §6.</ref>

==Calibrated submanifolds==

A ''p''-dimensional submanifold ''&Sigma;'' of ''M'' is said to be a '''calibrated submanifold''' with respect to ''&phi;'' (or simply ''&phi;''-calibrated) if ''&phi;''|<sub>''&Sigma;''</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;vol<sub>''&Sigma;''</sub>.  Equivalently, T''&Sigma;'' lies in ''G''(''&phi;'').

A famous one-line argument shows that calibrated closed submanifolds minimize volume within their [[Homology (mathematics)|homology class]]. Indeed, suppose that ''&Sigma;'' is calibrated, and ''&Sigma;''&prime; is a submanifold in the same homology class. Then
<math display="block">\int_\Sigma \mathrm{vol}_\Sigma = \int_\Sigma \varphi = \int_{\Sigma'} \varphi \leq \int_{\Sigma'} \mathrm{vol}_{\Sigma'},</math>
where the first equality holds because ''&Sigma;'' is calibrated, the second equality is [[Generalized Stokes' theorem|Stokes' theorem]] (as ''&phi;'' is closed), and the inequality holds because ''&phi;'' has operator norm 1.

The same argument shows that even a noncompact calibrated submanifold is a [[minimal submanifold]] in the variational sense, and therefore has zero [[mean curvature]].

In particular, [[affine variety|affine complex algebraic varieties]] are locally area-minimizing.  Federer used this to give some of the first examples of singular minimal submanifolds, such as the [[algebraic curve]] <math>\{w^2=z^3\} \subset \mathbb{C}^2</math>.<ref name="Federer"/><ref name="Morgan"/>

==Examples==

* On a [[Kähler manifold]], suitably normalized powers of the [[Kähler form]] are calibrations, and the calibrated submanifolds are the [[complex submanifold]]s.  This follows from the [[Wirtinger inequality (2-forms)|Wirtinger inequality]].
* On a [[Calabi–Yau manifold]], the real part of a holomorphic volume form (suitably normalized) is a calibration, and the calibrated submanifolds are [[special Lagrangian submanifold]]s.
* On a [[G2 manifold|G<sub>2</sub>-manifold]], both the parallel 3-form and its Hodge dual 4-form define calibrations. The corresponding calibrated submanifolds are called associative and coassociative submanifolds.
* On a [[Spin(7)-manifold]], the defining 4-form, known as the Cayley form, is a calibration. The corresponding calibrated submanifolds are called Cayley submanifolds.
